title: Precision morphing kernel selection + fallback policy and prefetch plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Dequantization and precision switching at decode time is a non-trivial per-request cost for mixed-precision serving. On short sequences and interactive workloads we see up to 18-25% of per-token CPU/GPU overhead coming from repeated format conversion and small-buffer copies during prefill/decode. Goal: Design and implement a runtime sub-system that morphs precision choice across the serving path (INT8 / FP8 / FP16) with a deterministic fallback policy that minimizes dequant overhead while preserving output fidelity and SLA tail-latency. Deliverables: 1) a kernel selection policy (Precision Morphing) that chooses the active execution lane at request admission + at key decode boundaries, 2) a fallback policy for unexpected latency pressure or correctness regression that switches to a compatible higher-precision kernel with minimal state movement, 3) a prefetch plan that aligns KV cache layout and attention tensors to avoid copies during precision transition, and 4) experiment results and perf regression guardrails for runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end p95 latency on chat workload (50-100 token responses) reduced by >=8% vs baseline when using INT8 path for compatible requests. 2) Dequant-related CPU/GPU overhead measured on profiling trace reduced by >=40% in typical mixed-precision cases. 3) No >0.5% degradation in log-prob delta for benchmark prompts vs FP16 baseline. 4) Fallback transitions complete without full KV serialization (zero-copy or single-page remap) in >=90% of cases.
implementation_notes: Design: - Admission-time scoring: quick heuristic that uses (model, seq_len, token_rate, customer tier) to pick INT8/FP8/FP16 lane. - Morph points: allow switching only at decode chunk boundaries (e.g., every 8 tokens) to amortize transition cost. - Fallback policy: two-stage fallback; soft-fallback (local cast view / ephemeral zero-copy cast for read-only attention slices) then hard-fallback (full per-layer recompute in FP16) if error budget exceeded. - Prefetch plan: schedule KV prefetch early for likely next-chunk heads and reserve contiguous pages for attention tensors to enable remap instead of copy. - Telemetry: add tags to requests indicating chosen lane, transition events, and bytes copied. Prototyped memory remap with cudaIpc-like page table trick; fallback still supports conservative copy on devices that disable remap. Implementation will live under runtime/kernel_manager and runtime/prefetch.
perf_results: Initial lab runs (A100x8): INT8 lane + morphing reduced decode-stage wall time by 22% and net per-token GPU kernel time by 11% on 64-token average responses. Dequant copy bandwidth reduced from 8.2GB/s to 1.6GB/s in best-case contiguous layout. p95 tail latency improved from 134ms -> 122ms on single-request baseline. Observed regressions: some attention-head ordering patterns cause remap-unfriendly layouts leading to 5-10ms spikes; tracked as follow-up.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Complexity: Kernel manager must maintain compatibility matrices for model sharding and per-layer numeric stability; increased code surface for bugs. - Remap portability: the zero-copy remap approach depends on GPU driver features; fallback copy path increases variability. - Quality: aggressive INT8 for all requests risks subtle distribution drift; must gate with per-customer rollout and eval set. - Observability: need fine-grained telemetry to catch regressions early, otherwise fallback will hide root causes.
